issue.title: Markdown: preserve newline around Chinese/Japanese characters not around Korean letters in all proseWrap settings
issue.body:
**Prettier de9ec361d**
[Playground link](https://prettier.io/playground/?version=next#N4Igxg9gdgLgprEAuEBRKBzANgSwM4AWAOlOtvsVIKemgNOaB5USbXUy-a825x9+7-Y-yiAdVcC2tYBbRkqIlRAtHKBw00CA-)
<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```sh
--parser markdown
--prose-wrap never
```

**Input:**
<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
English
English
日本語
日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語
日本語
한국어
한국어
中文！
한국어
```

**Output:**
<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
English English日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語 한국어 한국어 中文！한국어

```

**Expected output:**
<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
English English
日本語
日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語日本語
日本語 한국어 한국어 中文！
한국어

```

**Why?**

Follow up of https://github.com/prettier/prettier/issues/16710 / https://github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/16691

Prettier differs from CSS (and individual browsers) in how line breaks around CJ characters are recognized (whether they are equivalent to spaces or can be removed). Furthermore, processing methods are not standardized among browsers. Therefore, Prettier should keep line breaks around CJ characters as they are, even if proseWrap is set to something other than preserve.

The exception is line breaks between a CJ letter (excluding punctuation) and a Korean letter, where the behavior already matches that of CSS and individual browsers (equivalent to a space).

In https://github.com/prettier/prettier/issues/14936 / https://github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/16805, line breaks between CJK characters and non-CJK characters, as well as between CJK punctuation and Korean letters, will be allowed to be converted to spaces when proseWrap is set to always or never.

Related:

- dprint-plugin-markdown / deno fmt: https://github.com/dprint/dprint-plugin-markdown/issues/120#issuecomment-2426757408

<!-- short explanation of expected output -->

issue.title: [3.9 regression] Markdown: $...$ parsed as inline math across code spans, deleting spaces
issue.body:
**Prettier 3.9.8** (regression introduced in **3.9.0**, last good version **3.8.5**)

[Playground link](https://prettier.io/playground/#-)

```sh
# Options:
--parser markdown --prose-wrap always --print-width 100
# (the space deletion in the first paragraph also reproduces with no options at all)
```

**Input:**

```markdown
**Uses $FOO** from `a.sh` and `b.sh`, plus `$BAR` from `c.sh`, before anything else runs here.

**Sourced-from-$DOTFILES files** - listed in `.stow-local-ignore`. They live only inside the repo
and are pulled in by `.zshrc` via `$DOTFILES` (which is set to `~/.dotfiles` in `.zshrc`). Key
examples: `exports.zsh`, `aliases.zsh`, `dirs.zsh`, `completions/`, `_plugins/loader.zsh`.
```

**Output:**

```markdown
**Uses $FOO** from `a.sh` and `b.sh`, plus `$BAR`from`c.sh`, before anything else runs here.

**Sourced-from-$DOTFILES files** - listed in `.stow-local-ignore`. They live only inside the repo
and are pulled in by `.zshrc` via `$DOTFILES`(which is set to`~/.dotfiles`in`.zshrc`). Key examples: `exports.zsh`, `aliases.zsh`, `dirs.zsh`, `completions/`, `_plugins/loader.zsh`.
```

**Expected output:**

```markdown
**Uses $FOO** from `a.sh` and `b.sh`, plus `$BAR` from `c.sh`, before anything else runs here.

**Sourced-from-$DOTFILES files** - listed in `.stow-local-ignore`. They live only inside the repo
and are pulled in by `.zshrc` via `$DOTFILES` (which is set to `~/.dotfiles` in `.zshrc`). Key
examples: `exports.zsh`, `aliases.zsh`, `dirs.zsh`, `completions/`, `_plugins/loader.zsh`.
```

**Why?**

Two things go wrong, both from the same cause.

Spaces get deleted. `` `$BAR` from `c.sh` `` comes back as `` `$BAR`from`c.sh` ``, and the second
paragraph loses four more the same way. That's content loss rather than reformatting, and the result is
stable, so running Prettier again doesn't bring them back and nothing warns you about it.

Prose stops wrapping. The last two lines of the second paragraph get joined into one 181 character line
and left there, well past the 100 I asked for. 3.8.5 wraps the same text correctly.

The cause is inline math. Since 3.9.0 a `$ ... $` pair gets matched straight across backtick code spans,
so everything between the `$` in `**Uses $FOO**` and the `$` in `` `$BAR` `` becomes a single `inlineMath`
node. `--debug-print-ast` on the first paragraph:

3.8.5:

```
['inlineCode', 'paragraph', 'root', 'strong', 'text']
```

3.9.8:

```
['inlineCode', 'inlineMath', 'paragraph', 'root', 'text']
inlineMath value: 'FOO** from `a.sh` and `b.sh`, plus `'
```

That explains both symptoms. The math node swallows the closing `**` and both opening backticks, which
re-pairs every backtick after it, so ` from ` parses as a code span instead of plain text and CommonMark
strips one padding space from each side of it. And since math content is atomic it can't be broken, so
any paragraph containing one of these bogus nodes can no longer be wrapped.

CommonMark gives code spans precedence over other inline constructs, so a math span shouldn't be able to
start or end in the middle of one. I'm guessing this came along with the micromark upgrade in #18277,
since 3.8.5 parses the same line as `strong` + `inlineCode` and leaves it alone.

Not specific to lists or to `proseWrap`, I hit it first in a numbered list and a plain paragraph behaves
the same. Pretty easy to run into in any docs that mention shell variables more than once in the same
paragraph, `$HOME`, `$PATH`, `$DOTFILES` and so on. Thanks!

Hi @Abdellox - I have a reproducing example in the playground and in the issue description. You can use these as baseline for reproducing the problem. The expected output is also there.

My environment:

Operating system: macOS 26 (Tahoe)
Node version: v24.18.0
PNPM version: 11.7.0
NPM version: 11.16.0
Prettier version: 3.9.8

Is there anything else I can provide?
